title: Intelligent routing and multimodal attachment contract

tiers.quick: Prefer speed and low cost after capability checks.
tiers.balanced: Prefer balanced intelligence, speed, and cost.

rules: Reject routes that lack a required input capability.
Keep explicit user model selection authoritative.
Keep a person-selected chat pinned until that person explicitly selects Auto; Settings Routing does not rewrite manual chats.
Apply Settings Routing to unassigned desk spawns, and let any explicit spawn provider, model, or target chat win.
Remove explicitly excluded providers, models, and bots before scoring automatic routes.
Persist structured routing exclusions on the worker and inherit them across every nested spawn; reject an explicitly named excluded identity before a provider call.
Penalize weekly overdraw and protected reserve only when capacity routing is enabled.
Prefer capable spare capacity only when spare preference is enabled.
Use local models only when local routing is enabled.
Record tier, winner, alternatives, capacity state, and reason on every automatic route.
Never merge credentials, subscriptions, contexts, or sandboxes across providers.
Exclude Watch-held routes before dispatch and show any approved fallback.
Require Kimi K3 image capability for visual UI and UX plan tasks unless the user overrides or accepts unavailability.
Choose the lowest sufficient supported reasoning effort from task complexity and risk; never hard-code every worker to high.

planRouting.visualRole: audit-only; implementation is handed to a separate coding worker

delivery.file: Inline safe text or an auditable source manifest.
delivery.document: Native PDF where supported; otherwise a source manifest.
delivery.audio: Native MP3/WAV only for declared compatible models; otherwise a manifest.
delivery.video: Source manifest plus representative image frames.

attachments.truthRule: The visible attachment label, persisted metadata, routed capability, and outbound representation must agree.

evalPolicy.liveProviderCalls: Use the smallest deterministic call needed to prove launch and identity.
evalPolicy.cascades: Use fewer low-cost models and stay within the orchestration contract limits.
evalPolicy.productionBoundary: The MiniMax evaluator policy does not override a real production run; production orchestration uses task-appropriate models, effort, capacity, and explicit user assignments.
